# How to translate this chunk

This file holds `items`, a list of `{"k", "ctx", "t"}`. `t` is English text
that a reader of an Indian app or website sees. `ctx` is the field it came
from, such as label, hint, button, documents, brief or title. Use it to judge
tone and length: a label stays short, a hint can be a sentence.

Write `{"items": [{"k": ..., "t": ...}, ...]}` to the path in `write_to`.
Keep every `k` unchanged and in the same order. Put the translation in `t`.
Leave out `ctx`. Do not add, merge, split or drop items.

## Keep these exactly as they are

- Placeholders and markup: `{0}`, `{name}`, `%s`, `%d`, `%1$s`, HTML tags, `\n`.
- Website addresses, e-mail addresses and links.
- Every number: phone and toll-free numbers, Aadhaar, account, IFSC, PAN, PIN
  codes, amounts, dates, percentages. Write digits as 0-9, the Western digits,
  in every language, including Urdu. People type these into forms that take
  Western digits.
- Acronyms people know in Latin letters: OTP, PAN, IFSC, UPI, KYC, e-KYC, DBT,
  BPL, APL, NFSA, PM-KISAN, SMS, PDF, ID.

## Names

- Product, app, portal and scheme names: transliterate them into the script so
  they read naturally. Keep any acronym inside them in Latin, so "APPSC
  portal" becomes APPSC followed by the word for portal.
- A button or menu label quoted from a website, such as 'Apply Online' or
  'Register', stays in English inside quotes. The reader has to find that exact
  English word on the screen.
- People and places in examples are transliterated, never replaced with other
  names.
- Government office titles are transliterated so the reader can say them at
  the counter: Tahsildar, Patwari, Talathi, Mamlatdar, BDO, Collector, Gram
  Panchayat. The language notes below give the usual local forms.

## Tone

Write for an ordinary person who may be elderly and may have had little
schooling. Use everyday spoken language, not heavy official vocabulary. Where
people really say the English word, write it in the script: online, form,
portal, login, mobile, bank, certificate, download, upload, app. Keep
instructions short and direct, in the form "do this".

"Gender" means sex (male or female). It is never the word for caste.

## Before you write

Check that you have the same number of items as the input and that every
number and placeholder came through. Write the whole file in ONE Write call,
as valid UTF-8 JSON with no `\u` escapes and nothing else in the file.

## Hindi (hi)

Script: Devanagari. Used in UP, MP, Bihar, Rajasthan, Haryana, HP, Uttarakhand,
Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh and Delhi, and understood across the north.
Tone: everyday spoken Hindi (Hindustani). Avoid Sanskritised official words.
Words: ऑनलाइन, फॉर्म, पोर्टल, लॉगिन, आधार, बैंक, मोबाइल, OTP, हेल्पलाइन,
सर्टिफिकेट, डाउनलोड, अपलोड.
UI: आवेदन करें (Apply), जमा करें (Submit), आगे (Next), पीछे (Back), खोजें (Search),
शेयर करें (Share), सेटिंग (Settings), भाषा (Language), मदद (Help).
Offices: तहसीलदार, पटवारी, ग्राम पंचायत, कलेक्टर, ब्लॉक विकास कार्यालय (BDO).
Gender: लिंग (never जाति). Money: रु. 6,000; रु. 8 लाख. September: सितंबर.

items.t: Get the income certificate from the tehsildar through a Setu or Aaple Sarkar Seva Kendra, or a BPL certificate if the family is on the BPL list, and keep the age proof and residence certificate ready.
Hand it to the talathi or at the tehsil's Sanjay Gandhi Yojana branch and take the acknowledgement. The talathi visits your home to check the papers and family income.

The tehsildar places the file before the Sanjay Gandhi Niradhar Anudan Yojana committee, which also decides Shravanbal cases every month. Approved names are put on the notice board and read in the gram sabha.
The pension starts from the month after approval is complete online and comes by DBT into your Aadhaar-linked account every month.
Give the life certificate each year when the tehsil asks. If the pension stopped, giving it in the same financial year restarts it.
Lek Ladki Yojana
Women and Child Development Department, Government of Maharashtra (ICDS Commissionerate)

Rs.1,01,000 in five instalments for a girl born on or after 1 April 2023 in a family with a yellow or orange ration card, paid at stages from her birth until she turns 18. It replaced the older Majhi Kanya Bhagyashree scheme. The parents apply through the anganwadi sevika, who fills in the form with them, uploads it to the scheme portal and gives a receipt. The money goes by DBT into a joint bank account of the girl and her mother.
Rs.1,01,000 in 5 parts: Rs.5,000 at birth, Rs.6,000 in Class 1, Rs.7,000 in Class 6, Rs.8,000 in Class 11, Rs.75,000 at 18
Girl born on or after 1 April 2023 to a family living in Maharashtra
The family holds a yellow or orange ration card and its yearly income is not more than Rs.1 lakh
Covers one or two daughters; if the family has a son and a daughter, the daughter gets it; twin girls at the second delivery both get it
For the 3rd instalment of the first child, or the 2nd instalment of the second child, the mother or father must give a family planning operation certificate
The bank account must be in Maharashtra; for the last Rs.75,000 the girl must be 18, unmarried and on the voter list
Girl's birth certificate (register the birth with the gram panchayat or municipality first)
Income certificate from the tehsildar showing yearly family income up to Rs.1 lakh
Attested copy of the yellow or orange ration card
Aadhaar of the parents, and of the girl (not needed for the first instalment)
First page of the passbook of the joint account of the girl and her mother
Proof of residence in Maharashtra
For later instalments: school bonafide certificate, family planning certificate, and at 18 her voter ID and a self-declaration that she is unmarried

The anganwadi sevika of your area, at the anganwadi centre. The application form is printed at the end of the scheme GR linked here (pages 9 to 12), and blank forms are also kept at every Child Development Project Officer (CDPO) office, the Zilla Parishad District Programme Officer's office and the District Women and Child Development Officer's office. Take the filled form with copies of the documents, carry the originals for checking, and ask the sevika for the signed receipt (pohoch pavti) at the bottom of the form. Apply the same way for each later instalment.

Choose first to fifth. Each later instalment needs a fresh form when the girl reaches that stage.
Register the girl's birth at the gram panchayat or municipal office and collect the birth certificate.

Keep ready the yellow or orange ration card (attested copy), an income certificate of up to Rs.1 lakh from the tehsildar, the parents' Aadhaar and the joint account passbook of the girl and her mother.
Go to your anganwadi centre. The sevika fills in the Lek Ladki form with you, ticks the document checklist, uploads it to the portal and gives you the signed receipt. Keep that receipt.

The anganwadi supervisor checks the papers and the CDPO sends the list to the District Programme Officer of the Zilla Parishad, who approves it. If anything is missing you are told in writing within 15 days and get one month (plus 10 days) to complete it; the whole process should finish within two months.
Once approved, Rs.5,000 is credited by DBT to the joint account of the girl and her mother.

Apply again through the anganwadi with the school bonafide certificate when she enters Class 1, Class 6 and Class 11, and at 18 for the Rs.75,000 with her voter ID and a declaration that she is unmarried.
If the family moves to another district, apply for the remaining instalments to the ICDS office of the new district.
Your anganwadi sevika or the taluka CDPO office; 181 (women's helpline)
Namo Shetkari Mahasanman Nidhi Yojana (Namo Shetkari)
Department of Agriculture, Government of Maharashtra (Commissionerate of Agriculture, Pune)

Rs.6,000 a year from the Maharashtra government to every farmer family that receives PM-Kisan, paid in three instalments of Rs.2,000 straight into the bank account. Together with PM-Kisan's Rs.6,000 that makes Rs.12,000 a year. There is no separate Namo form: the state pays everyone who is eligible for the PM-Kisan instalment, so a farmer not yet on PM-Kisan registers on the PM-Kisan portal, and a farmer already on it who is not getting Namo money checks the status on nsmny.mahait.org and fixes the fault shown. An increase was announced in 2025, so check the portal for the rate in force.
Rs.6,000 a year (3 x Rs.2,000), on top of PM-Kisan's Rs.6,000
Farmer family in Maharashtra that is registered and found eligible under PM-Kisan; whoever qualifies for a PM-Kisan instalment gets the Namo instalment too
Cultivable land in the farmer's own name on the 7/12 extract, with the land seeded on the PM-Kisan record
PM-Kisan e-KYC done, and an Aadhaar-seeded bank account switched on for DBT
Farmer ID (Agristack) is needed for a new PM-Kisan registration

Same exclusions as PM-Kisan: income-tax payers, serving or retired government employees (Class IV staff excepted), pensioners getting Rs.10,000 or more a month, practising doctors, engineers, lawyers, CAs and architects, and holders of constitutional posts
7/12 extract and 8A of the land in your name
Mutation entry (ferfar), if the land came to you by inheritance
Bank passbook of an account seeded with Aadhaar and enabled for DBT
Mobile number linked to Aadhaar, for OTP and e-KYC
Farmer ID (Agristack number), made free at a CSC or through the talathi or krushi sahayak
Choose Rural Farmer if your land is in a village; Urban Farmer only if it lies within municipal limits.
Your own 12-digit Aadhaar. It is checked with UIDAI before the form opens.
Best if it is the number linked to your Aadhaar, because the OTP and later e-KYC use it.
Maharashtra
The state where your land is. The portal then checks whether your Farmer ID exists; if not, it offers the steps to make one.
Farmer ID (Agristack)
Get it made first at a CSC or through the talathi with Aadhaar and 7/12. Without it the registration does not go through.
Sanjay Maruti Pawar
Exactly as on Aadhaar. If the 7/12 spells it differently, get one of them corrected, or the land check fails.
Jalna / Ambad / Wadigodri
The village where the land is, as written on the 7/12.
Gat / survey number and area (from 7/12)
Gat No. 212/2, 1.20 hectares
Copy both from your 7/12 extract. Add every piece of land you hold in your own name.
An account in your own name that is seeded with Aadhaar at the bank. Both PM-Kisan and Namo money come here.
The 11 characters printed on the first page of the passbook.

If you already receive PM-Kisan, do not apply again. Open nsmny.mahait.org and use Beneficiary Status to see your Namo instalments; if one failed, the error-code table on the same page says what to do, such as re-seeding Aadhaar at the bank.
If you are not on PM-Kisan, first get your Farmer ID (Agristack) made at a CSC (Aaple Sarkar Seva Kendra) or through the talathi or krushi sahayak, taking Aadhaar and the 7/12.
Open the PM-Kisan New Farmer Registration form, choose Rural Farmer, enter Aadhaar, mobile and the state Maharashtra, and verify with the OTP.
Fill in your name, address, land details from the 7/12 and bank details, upload the 7/12, submit, and note the registration number shown.
The talathi and the taluka agriculture office check the land record, and the state approves it. Finish e-KYC on the portal by OTP or by face authentication.
Once you are approved for PM-Kisan, the Namo instalments follow automatically: Rs.2,000 three times a year, usually soon after each PM-Kisan instalment.
If payments stop, check the status on both portals. The usual causes are pending e-KYC, Aadhaar not seeded with the bank, or land not seeded; the taluka agriculture office can fix the last one.
020-25538755 (Namo Shetkari cell, Commissionerate of Agriculture, Pune); 155261 / 1800-115-526 (PM-Kisan helpline)
Maharashtra Construction Worker Registration (Bandhkam Kamgar Card, MAHABOCW)
Maharashtra Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board, Industries, Energy, Labour and Mining Department

Registration with the state construction workers' welfare board, which opens about 29 schemes for the worker and family: scholarships for two children, Rs.30,000 for the worker's first marriage, Rs.51,000 for a daughter's marriage, help to build or buy a house, Rs.5 lakh if the worker dies in a site accident and Rs.2 lakh on natural death. Since August 2025 registration and renewal cost nothing. You apply online on the board's portal, pick a date, and go once to your taluka construction workers' facilitation centre with the original papers for photo and fingerprint. Manipur's free health cover for poor families: up to Rs.5 lakh a year per family for hospital treatment, cashless at empanelled hospitals in Manipur and at chosen hospitals in Guwahati and Kolkata. It covers AAY card holders, widows, persons with disability, ASHAs, Anganwadi workers and helpers, Ima Keithel women vendors, newspaper hawkers, local media persons, displaced persons, and other poor families approved by the Deputy Commissioner. The card is made at the CMHT enrolment kiosk of a district hospital, and the scheme also pays travel fare and a daily allowance for treatment outside the state. It was launched in 2018 with Rs.2 lakh cover, now raised to Rs.5 lakh.
